source_review.notes: Reviewed Fagin et al., Litwin, Graefe, the cited textbook, current PostgreSQL 18 hash/index documentation and hash source/design notes, and current MySQL 8.4 MEMORY/hash guidance. Five online primary or official destinations returned HTTP 200. ACM, Microsoft, and both MySQL destinations returned automated-access HTTP 403; their primary/official content remained research-index readable. Product behavior is version/current-source scoped.

evidence: Checked equality relation ~, encoding E, hash H, metadata M, bucket function f, entry/bucket/capacity/load quantities, extendible global/local depths, and linear level/split pointer.
Checked code collision, bucket collision, logical duplicate, and MVCC version as distinct concepts.
Checked low-bit convention consistently across prose, executable model, examples, and exercises.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The requirement a~b implies equal compatible hashes is stated; the invalid converse is repeatedly rejected.

evidence: Independently recomputed directory A,B,C,B at depth 2 after inserting 0,2,4 and A,B,C,B,D,B,C,B at depth 3 after 6,8.
Independently recomputed B's local-depth split without directory doubling as A,B,C,E,D,B,C,E after inserting 1,3,5.
Recomputed reference counts 2^(g-d), low-bit signatures, key routing, and successful lookup set (0,1,2,3,4,5,6,8).
Recomputed the five-split linear-hash state N=2,i=1,p=3 and routes for codes 0 through 11.
numerical_recomputation.notes: A separate arithmetic program printed directory_invariants=True and linear_routes=True.

evidence: Re-derived extendible reference count as 2^(g-d) and why directory doubling preserves all unaffected bucket mappings.
Re-derived local split as refinement by bit d, redirecting half the old references and redistributing the entire old bucket.
Re-derived linear lookup's two cases from whether h_i(code) is below the split pointer.
Re-derived why completion of a linear split round permits incrementing level and resetting the pointer.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Expected constant access is explicitly conditional on distribution/load and does not replace worst-case linear candidate analysis.

evidence: Reviewed empty/missing key, exact capacity, first/global directory doubling, local-depth-only split, end-of-linear-round transition, and optional shrink/merge policy.
Reviewed full-code and bucket collisions, massive duplicates, NULL, case/collation normalization, composite encoding ambiguity, maximum keys, hash/seed/version upgrade, and index rebuild.
Reviewed long/cyclic overflow chains, stale metadata, concurrent old/new split visibility, partial movement, cleanup, crash replay, active pins, page generation, and reuse.
Reviewed adversarial chosen keys, secret reproducibility, hot buckets, low average load with bad tails, resource bounds, and sensitive telemetry.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Product/operator NULL and equality behavior is never inferred solely from generic hashing.

evidence: The repository verifier matched exact five-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status.
The executable validator checks directory size, local-depth bound, capacity, exact directory reference count, shared low-bit prefix, and routing of every stored key.
Independent checks reproduced directory reference and linear-routing invariants.
Draft validation accepted front matter, section order, ten examples, five exercises/answers, local links, and snippet execution before stopping only for this digest-bound record.
invariant_checking.notes: The model deliberately omits persistent pages, linear hashing, duplicates, SQL/MVCC, concurrency, WAL, attacks, and deletion.

evidence: Reviewed extendible stable-state coverage before and after directory doubling and local split.
Reviewed linear address partition between already-split buckets below p and unsplit buckets at/above p.
Reviewed collision/equality recheck necessity from the one-way hash compatibility implication.
Reviewed all exercise answers for directory arithmetic, split-round arithmetic, semantic encoding, recovery state, and experimental controls.
proof_review.notes: No proof of concurrency linearizability, recovery implementation, collision resistance, starvation freedom, optimizer choice, or workload performance is claimed.

evidence: The extendible correctness argument is explicitly labeled a stable-state proof sketch with excluded operational obligations.
The executable artifact is explicitly labeled an extendible teaching model, not PostgreSQL's linear-style implementation.
PostgreSQL split flags and no-shrink behavior are scoped to its current implementation; textbook merge remains optional policy.
Audited correct, exactly, direct, constant, stable, persistent, current, guarantees, proof, and secure language for scope.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The chapter distinguishes expected complexity, implementation mechanism, product capability, and empirical performance.

evidence: The standard-library extendible model executed successfully through the repository verifier.
A separately coded arithmetic check reproduced directory and linear-hash exercise results.
Five primary/official online destinations were retrieved; four automated requests returned HTTP 403 and are recorded.
Hash-versus-tree and security/performance conclusions are framed as experiments or conditional mechanisms, not measured universal results.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No live DBMS, disk bucket, MVCC history, concurrent split, WAL recovery, hostile traffic, or benchmark was executed.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter derives hash lookup from equality compatibility and cleanly separates codes, buckets, pages, dynamic address schemes, split protocols, logical visibility, and cost assumptions.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed overflow tails, extendible/linear growth, current PostgreSQL state/WAL behavior, metadata caches, hash/collation versioning, adversarial collisions, cleanup/reuse, observability, and access-path experiments.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review sheet, executable directory trace, ten distinct examples, and five exercises progress from semantic compatibility and routing arithmetic to concurrent recovery design and evidence-based index choice.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/official-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. The chapter does not certify a hash/equality implementation, DBMS access method, collation/NULL policy, concurrency or recovery protocol, adversarial resistance, workload result, or production fitness.
